title: Evolutionary algorithms can design novel living organisms built from frog cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolutionary algorithms can design novel living organisms built from frog cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A pipeline in which an evolutionary algorithm designs candidate organisms in silico for a desired function, and transferable designs are then built from Xenopus cells with a cell-based construction toolkit, can produce novel living systems that show the predicted behaviours, though some steps still need manual intervention.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Here we show a scalable pipeline for creating functional novel lifeforms: AI methods automatically design diverse candidate lifeforms in silico to perform some desired function, and transferable designs are then created using a cell-based construction toolkit to realize living systems with the predicted behaviors.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Abstract”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryonic epidermal and cardiac progenitor tissue shaped into designed aggregates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The design-to-build pipeline and behavioral transfer have direct measurable endpoints. Published supplementary material permits substantial checking, but limited designs and incomplete raw experimental data leave scalability only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare simulated performance and predicted behavior for each design with blinded trajectory and task measurements from its constructed counterpart, and test whether transfer exceeds control or random designs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The broad scalability claim exceeds the small demonstrated design set.

Complete raw videos and measurements may not be openly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The in silico design loop is specified and the code was deposited for reproduction, so that half can be re-run. The claim also requires living Xenopus builds to show the predicted behaviors, and those trajectories were published as summaries and supplementary media rather than as a downloadable track dataset. Existing materials can test the computational half and only audit the biological half.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run the deposited evolutionary pipeline for a stated objective and compare simulated behavior with the published living builds; transfer holds if built designs show the targeted behavior and shape-scrambled builds do not.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Manual construction steps mean a simulator re-run does not test the living half of the pipeline.

The paper deposits computational code only; Ethovision tracks and build videos are not in an open measurement archive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
